Cornbread Stuffing

Served at: Thanksgiving Day (United States)

Serves 8Prep 30 minCook 45 min

Cornbread stuffing is a classic side dish traditionally served at Thanksgiving in the United States. It combines the sweet, crumbly texture of cornbread with savory herbs and vegetables, making it a beloved complement to turkey and other holiday dishes.

Ingredients

  • 8 cups crumbled cornbread (about 1 lb or 450 g)
  • 1 cup chopped onion (about 150 g)
  • 1 cup chopped celery (about 120 g)
  • 1/2 cup unsalted butter (1 stick or 113 g)
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 teaspoons dried sage
  • 1 teaspoon dried thyme
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
  • 2 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken broth (600 ml)
  • 2 large eggs, beaten
  • 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
  2. In a large skillet, melt the butter over medium heat.
  3. Add the chopped onion, celery, and garlic to the skillet and sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
  4. In a large mixing bowl, combine the crumbled cornbread, sautéed vegetables, dried sage, dried thyme, salt, pepper, and fresh parsley if using.
  5. In a separate bowl, whisk together the chicken broth and beaten eggs.
  6. Pour the broth and egg mixture over the cornbread mixture and gently toss to combine, ensuring the cornbread is moist but not soggy.
  7. Transfer the mixture to a greased 9x13-inch (23x33 cm) baking dish and spread evenly.
  8. Bake uncovered for 40-45 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the stuffing is heated through.
  9. Remove from oven and let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, use homemade cornbread or add cooked sausage to the sautéed vegetables.
  • If you prefer a moister stuffing, add an extra 1/4 cup (60 ml) of chicken broth.
  • To make it vegetarian, substitute vegetable broth for chicken broth and use butter or olive oil.
